notice: RN bank batch 128: Mental health case studies: depression with suicide risk, lithium toxicity, NMS and clozapine. Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026. See REVIEW-LOG.md. Also carries the bank-wide catalog (catalog.py): the RN Question Bank and every curated test set.

questions.stem: Highlight the findings that raise this client's immediate suicide risk.

rationale.correct: A plan, means, prior attempt, alcohol and sudden calm early in treatment signal high risk.

perOption.r1: A specific plan with access to lethal means.
perOption.r3: Energy returns before mood lifts; a decision may have been made.
perOption.r6: Antidepressants carry a boxed warning for suicidality under 25.

references: Psychiatric-mental health nursing texts (e.g. Varcarolis; Halter)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Recognize cues of high suicide risk.

questions.stem: For each statement, indicate whether it is accurate or inaccurate about suicide risk.

rows.text: Asking directly about suicide does not plant the idea
Risk can rise in the first weeks of antidepressant treatment
A sudden improvement in mood can mean a decision to die
A no-suicide contract makes the client safe
Clients who talk about suicide rarely act on it

rationale.correct: Direct questions are safe; contracts are not protective.

perOption.r1:c1: Direct questions are safe and expected.
perOption.r1:c2: Direct questions are safe and expected.

references: Psychiatric-mental health nursing texts (e.g. Varcarolis; Halter)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Analyze suicide risk myths and facts.

questions.stem: Complete the sentence by choosing from the lists of options.

content.template: The priority nursing problem is {{b1}}, so the client needs {{b2}}.

options.text: imminent risk of suicide
sleep disturbance
social isolation
knowledge deficit about sertraline
one-to-one observation within arm's length
checks every 30 minutes
a private room with the door closed
an outpatient appointment next week

rationale.correct: Imminent risk needs continuous close observation.

questions.stem: Which interventions should the nurse include on admission? Select all that apply.

options.text: Search belongings for items that could be used for self-harm
Remove belts, cords and shoelaces
Check that the client swallows each medicine
Ask the client to promise to tell staff before acting
Allow a private bathroom with a locked door for dignity

rationale.correct: Environmental safety, removal of means and medication checks.

perOption.d: A no-harm contract is not a safety measure.

references: Psychiatric-mental health nursing texts (e.g. Varcarolis; Halter)

exhibits.title: Orders
exhibits.body: One-to-one observation. Sertraline continued. Collaborative safety plan before any discharge.

questions.stem: On day 2, the client says, "Everyone would be better off without me." Which responses by the nurse are therapeutic? Select all that apply.

options.text: "Are you thinking about killing yourself right now?"
"You feel like a burden to the people around you."
"I'm going to stay with you. Tell me more about that."
"Don't say that. Your family loves you very much."
"Why would you think something like that about yourself?"

rationale.correct: Ask directly, reflect and stay present.

perOption.e: "Why" questions put the client on the defensive.

references: Psychiatric-mental health nursing texts (e.g. Varcarolis; Halter)

exhibits.title: Day 2
exhibits.body: Client sitting alone in the dayroom; one-to-one staff present.

questions.stem: On day 9, the team considers discharge. For each finding, indicate whether it supports discharge or needs follow-up first.

rows.text: Can name warning signs and three people to call
Roommate has removed the oxycodone from the dorm
"I'll be fine once I'm out. I don't need the crisis line number."
Outpatient appointment within 7 days of discharge
Says the thoughts come but leave quickly and has no plan

rationale.correct: A safety plan, means restriction and early follow-up support discharge; refusing the crisis plan does not.

perOption.r5:c1: The period after discharge is high risk.
perOption.r5:c2: The period after discharge is high risk.

questions.stem: For each factor, select how it raised the lithium level. Each row may have more than one answer.

rationale.correct: Dehydration, low sodium and NSAIDs all raise lithium.

perOption.r1:c1: Dehydration and sodium loss make the kidneys hold lithium.
perOption.r1:c2: Dehydration and sodium loss make the kidneys hold lithium.

content.template: The nurse should first {{b1}}, and the provider is likely to order {{b2}}.

options.text: hold the next lithium dose and notify the provider
give the dose with food
give the PRN haloperidol for confusion
encourage the client to rest
IV 0.9% sodium chloride and preparation for hemodialysis if it worsens
activated charcoal
a low-sodium diet
furosemide

exhibits.body: Hold lithium. 0.9% sodium chloride 150 mL/hr. Repeat level in 6 hours. Nephrology consult.

Allow the client to walk alone to the group room
Restrict fluids to 1 liter a day

rationale.correct: Falls, seizures and fluid status need close attention.

questions.educationalObjective: Take action for safety in lithium toxicity.

questions.stem: At discharge, for each statement, indicate whether it shows understanding or needs more teaching.

rows.text: "I'll drink 2 to 3 liters of water a day and more in hot weather."
"I'll keep my salt intake about the same each day."
"If I get vomiting or diarrhea, I'll call my provider."
"Ibuprofen is fine for my back pain."
"I'll get my thyroid and kidney blood tests as scheduled."
"I'll start a low-salt diet to lose weight."

rationale.correct: Steady fluids and salt, avoid NSAIDs and keep lab tests.

perOption.r4:c1: NSAIDs raise lithium; acetaminophen is preferred.
perOption.r4:c2: NSAIDs raise lithium; acetaminophen is preferred.

references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information

questions.stem: Highlight the findings that suggest neuroleptic malignant syndrome (NMS).

references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information

questions.stem: For each feature, indicate whether it favors NMS or serotonin syndrome.

rows.text: Onset over days after a dopamine blocker
Onset within hours of a serotonergic drug
Clonus and hyperreflexia, worse in the legs

rationale.correct: Timing, rigidity versus clonus and drug class separate the two.
references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information

restrain the client
dantrolene or bromocriptine with cooling and IV fluids
a second antipsychotic

questions.stem: The client is moved to the ICU. Which interventions should the nurse anticipate? Select all that apply.

options.text: Cooling blankets and ice packs
IV fluids with urine output monitoring
Cardiac monitoring
Aspiration precautions
Acetaminophen as the main way to lower the temperature
Restart haloperidol at a lower dose tomorrow

rationale.correct: Cooling, fluids, monitoring and aspiration precautions.

perOption.e: Central fever does not respond well.
perOption.f: Wait at least 2 weeks and choose another agent.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)

questions.stem: The client was admitted involuntarily. In the ICU, the client remains confused. Which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.

options.text: Continue emergency treatment of NMS
Involve the legally authorized representative in decisions
Document the client's capacity assessment
Assume involuntary admission removes all rights to refuse treatment
Delay NMS treatment until a court order is obtained

rationale.correct: Emergency care proceeds; involuntary status does not remove rights.

perOption.a: Emergency treatment is allowed to save life.
perOption.d: Clients keep rights; refusal is handled through legal processes.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment

questions.stem: Complete the sentence by choosing from the lists of options.

content.template: With an ANC of 900 and a fever, the nurse should {{b1}}, and the client needs {{b2}}.

options.text: hold clozapine and notify the prescriber today
double the clozapine to keep the voices away
continue clozapine and recheck in a month
switch to a laxative only
urgent assessment for infection and bowel obstruction
a routine visit next month
a sleep study
a dental cleaning

rationale.correct: Hold clozapine and assess for infection and obstruction.

questions.stem: Which parts of the long-term clozapine plan should the nurse include? Select all that apply.

options.text: Regular ANC monitoring per the schedule
A bowel regimen with a stimulant laxative
Weight, glucose and lipids
Tell the prescriber before stopping smoking
Use bulk-forming fiber alone for constipation
Stop clozapine for 2 weeks if a dose is missed and restart at the old dose

rationale.correct: ANC checks, a bowel plan, metabolic checks and alerting the prescriber about smoking changes.

perOption.d: Smoking lowers clozapine levels; quitting can cause toxicity.
perOption.e: Can worsen obstruction with slow transit.
perOption.f: Must be re-titrated after missed days.

references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information

questions.stem: The client is admitted to a medical unit where staff are unfamiliar with clozapine. Which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

options.text: Tell the team that missed doses longer than 48 hours require re-titration

Leave the psychiatric history out of the handoff for privacy

caseStudies.title: Major depression with suicide risk early in SSRI treatment

exhibits.title: Admission to the mental health unit
exhibits.body: A 19-year-old college student with major depressive disorder started sertraline 12 days ago. Today the student's roommate brought the student in after finding a goodbye note. The student says, "I have more energy now, and I finally know what I need to do." The student has given away a guitar and a laptop this week.

rows.label: Plan
cells: Will take a bottle of the roommate's pills

rows.label: Columbia scale
cells: Positive for intent and preparatory behavior

rows.label: Alcohol
cells: Drinking alone most nights for 2 weeks

exhibits.title: Mental health unit, day 6
exhibits.body: A 42-year-old client admitted with acute mania takes lithium 900 mg twice daily. The client had a stomach virus with vomiting and diarrhea for 2 days and started ibuprofen for a sore back. Today the client is unsteady and has slurred speech.

exhibits.title: Mental health unit
exhibits.body: A 34-year-old client with schizophrenia was admitted 4 days ago with agitation and received haloperidol IM several times plus oral haloperidol. Today the client is stiff, sweaty and not answering questions.

exhibits.title: Clozapine clinic
exhibits.body: A 29-year-old client with treatment-resistant schizophrenia started clozapine 10 weeks ago. Voices have quieted for the first time in years. Today the client reports a sore throat and has not had a bowel movement in 5 days. The client smokes 20 cigarettes a day and plans to quit.

testSets.title: NCLEX-RN adaptive exam
testSets.description: Works like the real NCLEX-RN: each question depends on your answers so far, and the exam stops once your result is clear, after 85 to 150 questions. Choose timed (5 hours) or untimed. No going back; answers and rationales at the end. The questions are being rewritten to real NCLEX difficulty and recalibrated, so treat your result as a practice estimate.
